correctness.rationale: Writing A_s=1+q+…+q^(s−1), the congruence for f^A_s follows by q-powering the previous congruence and multiplying by f: at least one exponent in terms from h reaches q^s, and the corner term is the unique survivor. For e=rs+t, 0≤t<r, the p^t-th power yields the survivor of exponent p^e−p^t in every variable, at power p^t A_s=floor((p^e−1)/(q−1)); the remainder in the division is p^t−1. Every monomial of f kills this survivor since q−1≥p^t. For s=0 the same formula is zero, since f is already in the ideal. This uses no perfectness assumption. At λ=0, for e≥r, qM=p^e and M=p^(e−r): F^M vanishes by Frobenius, whereas distributing M−1 nearly equally between two variables gives a surviving monomial by Lucas and the strict exponent inequality. The tangent form has degree q+1<n(q−1) and smooth projectivization; its partials are x_i^q. Those remain the initial forms of the deformed partials. Their regular sequence has only Koszul first syzygies, so cancellation of leading terms in a Jacobian-ideal representation lifts through those syzygies; the initial ideal is generated by these pure powers. Its colength q^n gives isolatedness and the stated Jacobian Milnor number. Independently reproduced 81 small exact quotient cases, including non-Fermat h and points across residue classes of e mod r, using repeated sparse multiplication; replay `python3 /workspace/branches/independent_reproduce.py` (section 1).
residual_risks: Finite cases do not certify arbitrary coefficients or e; the Frobenius and filtered-regular-sequence arguments establish these quantifiers.
